tool.name: dex_search_contacts
tool.title: Search Contacts
tool.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone number, or any keyword. Phone numbers are matched on digits; formatting and country code are ignored (a query that is only a phone number searches phone numbers instead of the text fields, so "+420 604 354 254", "420604354254" and "604354254" all find the same contact). Use `near` for geographic proximity ("contacts in the Bay Area", "near Sydney") — the place is geocoded and contacts are matched by their own coordinates, so it finds people whose saved location differs from the query (e.g. "San Francisco" still matches "Bay Area"). `near` and `query` combine (AND): "engineers in the Bay Area" → query "engineer" + near "Bay Area". Returns up to `limit` results. Use an empty query to list contacts sorted by most recently interacted.

near.description: Geographic proximity search: a place to find contacts near ("Bay Area", "Sydney", "Austin, TX"). Matches contacts by their coordinates within `radius_km`.

query.description: Search query (name, company, job title, phone number, etc.). A phone number is matched on its digits only — pass it in any formatting, with or without the country code. Use empty string to list all contacts. When `near` is set, use this ONLY for an additional non-location filter to narrow within the area (e.g. "engineer", "Google") — leave it empty for everyone nearby, and do NOT repeat the place name here (that over-filters).

radius_km.description: Radius in km around `near` (default 50). Use a larger value for a region/state, smaller for a neighbourhood.

"unset" simply clears the cadence so the contact has none — "no cadence", "remove the keep-in-touch" — leaving them unmarked rather than flagged. Every value overwrites whatever cadence each contact already has — and "never"/"unset" leave nothing in its place — so confirm with the user before changing a large set. Marking a due keep-in-touch as done is dex_complete_keep_in_touch, not this tool.

tool.name: dex_research_contacts
tool.title: Research Contacts on the Web
tool.description: Run Dex Research on 1–5 contacts: searches the public web, reads the best pages, and stores a cited research note per contact (one-line summary + "Current focus" / "Background" / "Interests" bullets with [[n]] citations into `sources`) plus structured findings (LinkedIn, website, email, phone) with confidence and evidence. This is a PAID action that takes a minute or more per contact (contacts run in parallel, so the call lasts as long as the slowest one) — confirm with the user before researching a large set, and chunk bigger sets into several calls. A contact researched within the last 30 days returns its cached note at no cost unless `force: true`. A run auto-fills a contact's EMPTY linkedin/website fields from high-confidence findings (reported in `applied`) and preserves populated contact fields; a fresh run replaces the previous stored research note, findings, and review statuses. Email/phone findings come back `pending` for the user to confirm before you apply them with dex_update_contact. `outcome: "in_progress"` means another request is already researching that contact: read it back later with dex_get_contact_research rather than running again. Results are large — research a few contacts per call to stay under the response limit. Rows that are not `ok` are listed first so they survive truncation; an `ok` note that was truncated is still stored and readable with dex_get_contact_research.

tool.name: dex_list_upcoming_reminders_and_birthdays
tool.title: List Upcoming Reminders, Birthdays and Keep in Touch
tool.description: What's coming up for the user inside a date window, like the Dex homepage: the contacts whose birthday falls in the window, the open reminders due in it, and the keep-in-touch contacts due for a touch by the end of it. Defaults to the next 7 days starting today — use `days: 30` for the next month, or set `from` to look at a specific week. Use this for questions like "whose birthday is next week?", "who should I reach out to this week?" or "what do I have coming up?". Recurring reminders are listed on their next occurrence. Birthdays the user already marked done this year on the homepage are omitted. `keep_in_touch` DOES include contacts already overdue for a touch (flagged `is_overdue`) — the homepage keeps showing them as due until the touch is logged. Overdue reminders are NOT included — call dex_list_reminders with is_overdue=true for those.
